title: Why It Costs More Than a Penny to Make a Penny
description:
The US penny has cost more to produce than it's actually worth for years running. Here's why, and why that math finally caught up with it.

Educational content, not financial advice.

#shorts #financefacts #money

scenes.text: For years, it has cost the US government more than one cent to make a single penny.
Most of that cost comes from the metal itself, mainly zinc with a thin copper coating, plus the cost of striking and shipping the coins.
The US Mint has reported a loss on every penny made for well over a decade, adding up to real money at billions of coins produced.
It's not just a US problem either. Canada eliminated its penny back in 2013 for the exact same reason.
When a coin costs more to make than it's worth, minting more of them is a losing trade by definition, no matter how small each loss looks.
That math is exactly why the US has been moving to wind down penny production altogether.
